However, if you follow certain guidelines during the move, you can usually remove a patient from a life-threatening situation without causing further injury to the patient. You can move a patient on his or her back along the floor or ground by using one of the following methods: Pull on the patient's clothing in the neck and shoulder area (FIGURE 8-14A).

highlight: If the shirt has buttons, the top two should be undone to prevent the patient from choking. Place the patient onto a blanket, coat, or other item that can be pulled (FIGURE 8-14B). Rotate the patient's arms so that they are extended straight on the ground beyond his or her head, grasp the wrists, and, with the arms elevated above the ground, drag the patient (FIGURE 814C). Place your arms under the patient's shoulders and through the armpits, and, while grasping your opposite wrist, drag the patient backward (FIGURE 8-14D).
